title: حِكَايَةُ صَاحِبِ الْجَزَائِرِ السُّودِ
titleEn: The Tale of the Lord of the Black Isles, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 48–54 (continuing directly from nights-07, whose text ends as the Sultan strikes down the black slave he finds with the young man's wife, believing him dead, just as dawn cuts Shahrazad off), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the project’s own two-pass-plus-adjudication pipeline; the edition’s own OCR is unusable. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition’s — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor’s slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized automatically once this file is published, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 8 continues directly from the young man's own account, mid-sentence, of the night he struck down the black slave he found in his wife's arms: he did not sever the great veins as he intended, only the windpipe, skin and flesh, and believed him dead until he heard him snore. His wife's grief that followed was staged: she claimed the deaths of her parents and brothers, built a domed “House of Sorrows” over the wounded slave under pretext of mourning, and tended and fed him there twice daily for nearly three years while ignoring her husband, exchanging bitter, mocking verses with him over the tomb when he finally confronted her. When he cursed her with the coarsest insults he could summon, she caught him raising his sword against her and, laughing, cast the spell that turned his lower body to stone, transformed the city's four religious communities into four colors of fish, and turned its surrounding islands into the four mountains ringing the enchanted pool — punishing him nightly with a hundred lashes ever since. Hearing this, the Sultan resolves to help: that night he secretly kills the still-living slave in his tomb, disguises himself in the slave's place, and when the sorceress comes to weep over “him” as usual, answers her in a feigned accent, complains that the young man's nightly cries for help disturb his own rest, and extracts her promise — “hearing and obedience” — to undo the curse. She restores the young man to his own form and drives him away, then, still believing she is speaking to her lover, turns to free the city itself, and is on her way to the pool with water to complete the spell's reversal when dawn cuts Shahrazad off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language toward Classical Arabic here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit. The night is frank about violence — the staged mourning, the whipping, the killing of the slave — and about coarse insult, and is translated that way.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāminatu qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīd
sentences.l: So when it was the eighth night, she said, "It has reached me, O fortunate king,
sentences.i: Now when the eighth night came, she said, "It has reached me, O fortunate King,

sentences.t: أَنَّ الشَّابَّ الْمَسْحُورَ قَالَ لِلْمَلِكِ لَمَّا ضَرَبْتُ الْعَبْدَ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ أَقْطَعَ رَأْسَهُ لَمْ أَقْطَعِ الْوَرِيدَيْنِ بَلْ قَطَعْتُ الْحُلْقُومَ وَالْجِلْدَ وَاللَّحْمَ فَظَنَنْتُ أَنِّي قَتَلْتُهُ
sentences.tr: anna al-shābba al-mashūra qāla li-al-maliki lammā ḍarabtu al-ʿabda li-ajli an aqṭaʿa raʾsahu lam aqṭaʿi al-warīdayni bal qaṭaʿtu al-ḥulqūma wa-al-jilda wa-al-laḥma fa-ẓanantu annī qataltuh
sentences.l: that the bewitched young man said to the king: When I struck the slave in order that I might cut off his head, I did not cut the two jugular-veins, but I cut the windpipe and the skin and the flesh, so I supposed that I had killed him.
sentences.i: that the bewitched young man said to the king: When I struck the slave meaning to cut off his head, I did not sever the two great veins of his neck, but only the windpipe, the skin, and the flesh — so I thought I had killed him.
sentences.n: مَسْحُور, 'bewitched', names what has already befallen this young man in the frame; the curse that leaves him half stone was set by his wife earlier in the night. أَقْطَعِ takes a helping kasra rather than its expected jussive sukūn because the next word opens with the elidable hamza of the definite article — Classical Arabic never lets two vowelless consonants stand next to each other.

sentences.t: فَشَخَرَ شَخِيرًا عَالِيًا فَتَحَرَّكَتْ بِنْتُ عَمِّي فَرَجَعْتُ إِلَى خَلْفِي وَ رَدَّيْتُ السَّيْفَ إِلَى مَوْضِعِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-shakhara shakhīran ʿāliyan fa-taḥarrakat bintu ʿammī fa-rajaʿtu ilā khalfī wa-raddaytu al-sayfa ilā mawḍiʿih
sentences.l: Then he snored a loud snore, and my paternal-cousin stirred, so I withdrew back and put the sword back in its place.
sentences.i: Then he gave a loud snore, and my cousin stirred; so I drew back and returned the sword to its place.
sentences.n: رَدَّيْتُ is this text's Middle Arabic conjugation of the doubled verb رَدَّ ('to put back') as though it were final-weak, giving raddaytu for the Classical raddadtu — a colloquial-leaning pattern (compare Night 7's سَبَتُّ) kept here as printed rather than repaired.

sentences.t: وَ أَنَيْتُ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ وَ دَخَلْتُ الْقَصْرَ وَ رَقَدْتُ فِي فِرَاشِي إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-anaytu ilā al-madīnati wa-dakhaltu al-qaṣra wa-raqadtu fī firāshī ilā al-ṣabāḥ
sentences.l: And I arrived at the city, and entered the palace, and lay down in my bed until the morning.
sentences.i: And I made my way to the city, went into the palace, and lay down in my bed till morning.
sentences.n: أَنَيْتُ is the classical verb أَنَى / يَأْنِي, 'to arrive, draw near' — a slightly elevated choice for 'I came', kept as the edition has it rather than read as the far commoner أَتَيْتُ.

sentences.t: وَ إِذَا بِنْتُ عَمِّي جَاءَتْ وَ نَبَّهَتْنِي وَ إِذَا بِهَا قَطَعَتْ شَعْرَهَا وَ لَبِسَتْ ثِيَابَ الْحُزْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bintu ʿammī jāʾat wa-nabbahatnī wa-idhā bihā qaṭaʿat shaʿrahā wa-labisat thiyāba al-ḥuzn
sentences.l: And behold, my paternal-cousin came and woke me; and behold her — she had cut her hair and put on the garments of mourning.
sentences.i: And behold, my cousin came and woke me; and there she was, her hair cut off and dressed in mourning garb.

sentences.t: وَ قَالَتْ يَا ابْنَ عَمِّي لَا تُعَارِضْنِي فِيمَا أَفْعَلُ فَإِنَّهُ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ وَالِدَتِي تُوُفِّيَتْ وَ أَنَّ وَالِدِي قُتِلَ فِي الْجِهَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat yā ibna ʿammī lā tuʿāriḍnī fīmā afʿalu fa-innahu balaghanī anna wālidatī tuwuffiyat wa-anna wālidī qutila fī al-jihād
sentences.l: And she said: O son of my uncle, do not oppose me in what I do; for it has reached me that my mother has died, and that my father was killed in the holy war.
sentences.i: And she said: O my cousin, do not cross me in what I do; for word has reached me that my mother has died, and that my father was slain fighting the holy war.

sentences.t: وَ إِخْوَتِي أَحَدُهُمْ مَاتَ مَلْسُوعًا وَ الْآخَرُ مَاتَ مُرْتَدِيًا فَيَحِقُّ لِي أَنْ أَبْكِيَ وَ أَحْزَنَ
sentences.tr: wa-ikhwatī aḥaduhum māta malsūʿan wa-al-ākharu māta murtadiyan fa-yaḥiqqu lī an abkiya wa-aḥzan
sentences.l: And as for my brothers — one of them died stung, and the other died fallen-to-ruin; so it is right for me that I weep and grieve.
sentences.i: And of my brothers, one died of a sting, and the other perished by a fall; so it is only right that I should weep and mourn.
sentences.n: مُرْتَدِيًا is printed exactly so — م ر ت د ي ا — and its sense is not certain. Read at face value (from اِرْتَدَى) it would mean 'clothed, wearing', which fits no manner of death; the translation here instead takes it as merging with تَرَدَّى / رَدِيَ, 'to fall to one's ruin, perish by a fall', which pairs sensibly with 'died stung' as a second accidental death. The word is vocalised as printed and the reading offered is a guess, on the model of Night 7's ورحاق.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَهَا سَكَتْتُ عَنْهَا وَ قُلْتُ افْعَلِي مَا بَدَا لَكِ فَإِنِّي لَمْ أُخَالِفْكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāmahā sakattu ʿanhā wa-qultu ifʿalī mā badā laki fa-innī lam ukhālifk
sentences.l: And when I heard her words, I fell silent toward her and said: Do as seems good to you, for I will not oppose you.
sentences.i: When I heard her words, I said nothing more to her, and told her: Do as you please, for I will not stand against you.

sentences.t: فَقَعَدَتْ فِي حُزْنٍ وَ بُكًى وَ عَلِيلٍ سَنَةً كَامِلَةً مِنَ الْحَوْلِ إِلَى الْحَوْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-qaʿadat fī ḥuznin wa-bukan wa-ʿalīlin sanatan kāmilatan mina al-ḥawli ilā al-ḥawl
sentences.l: So she sat in grief and weeping and sickness a whole year, from the year's-turn to the year's-turn.
sentences.i: So she sat in grief and weeping and sickness a full year, from one year's end to the next.
sentences.n: بُكًى is a recognised variant spelling of بُكَاء, 'weeping' (read bukan), matching the printed rasm exactly rather than being an error.

sentences.t: وَ بَعْدَ السَّنَةِ قَالَتْ لِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبْنِيَ لِي فِي قَصْرِكَ مَدْفَنًا مِثْلَ الْقُبَّةِ وَ أُفْرِدُهُ لِلْحُزْنِ وَ أُسَمِّيهِ بَيْتَ الْأَحْزَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda al-sanati qālat lī urīdu an tabniya lī fī qaṣrika madfanan mithla al-qubbati wa-ufriduhu li-al-ḥuzni wa-usammīhi bayta al-aḥzān
sentences.l: And after the year, she said to me: I want you to build me, in your palace, a burial-place like a dome, and I set it apart for mourning and I name it the House of Sorrows.
sentences.i: And after the year had passed, she said to me: I want you to build me, in your palace, a tomb like a dome, which I shall set apart for mourning and call the House of Sorrows.
sentences.n: Her plan shifts the actor mid-sentence — 'that you build' but 'I devote... I name' — printed exactly this way rather than smoothed into one consistent person.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا افْعَلِي مَا بَدَا لَكِ فَبَنَتُ لَهَا بَيْنًا لِلْحُزْنِ وَ بَنَتُ فِي وَسَطِهِ قُبَّةً وَ مَدْفَنًا مِثْلَ الضَّرِيحِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā ifʿalī mā badā laki fa-banat lahā baynan li-al-ḥuzni wa-banat fī wasaṭihi qubbatan wa-madfanan mithla al-ḍarīḥ
sentences.l: So I said to her: Do as seems good to you. So I built for her a 'bayn' for mourning, and built in its midst a dome and a burial-place like a shrine.
sentences.i: So I told her: Do as you please. So I built her a house set apart for mourning, and built within it a dome and a burial-place like a tomb.
sentences.n: بَيْنًا is printed ب ي ن ا, which as it stands would only mean 'an interval, a between' — not a sensible object for 'I built'. The sense plainly wants بَيْتًا, 'a house', and that is how it is rendered in the idiomatic line, but the letters are kept exactly as the edition has them rather than silently corrected. بنت (twice in this line) is spelled with the three letters of the regular 3fs 'she built' (بَنَتْ), but the sense — the narrator carrying out what he was just asked to do — calls for the 1cs 'I built'; it is read and translated that way, on the working assumption that this is the same kind of contracted first-person spelling seen in رَدَّيْتُ above.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَقَلْتُ الْعَبْدَ وَ أَنْزَلْتُهُ فِيهِ وَ هُوَ بَقِيَ لَا يَنْفَعُهَا أَبَدًا بِنَافِعَةٍ لَكِنْ يَشْرَبُ الشَّرَابَ
sentences.tr: thumma naqaltu al-ʿabda wa-anzaltuhu fīhi wa-huwa baqiya lā yanfaʿuhā abadan bi-nāfiʿatin lākin yashrabu al-sharāb
sentences.l: Then I moved the slave and lodged him in it, and he remained of no use to her at all, with no use — but he drinks the drink.
sentences.i: Then I had the slave moved and laid him inside it; he remained of no use to her at all — yet he still took drink.

sentences.t: وَ مِنْ يَوْمِ جَرَحْتُهُ مَا تَكَلَّمَ لِأَنَّ أَجَلَهُ مَا فَرَغَ
sentences.tr: wa-min yawmi jaraḥtuhu mā takallama li-anna ajalahu mā faragh
sentences.l: And from the day I wounded him he did not speak, because his appointed term had not run out.
sentences.i: And from the day I wounded him he had not spoken, for his allotted term had not yet run its course.

sentences.t: وَ صَارَتْ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَأْتِيهِ بُكْرَةً وَ عَشِيًّا تَنْزِلُ إِلَى الْقُبَّةِ وَ تَبْكِي وَ تُعَدِّدُ عَلَيْهِ وَ تَسْقِيهِ الشَّرَابَ وَ الْمَسَالِيقَ بُكْرَةً وَ عَشِيَّةً
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārat kulla yawmin taʾtīhi bukratan wa-ʿashiyyan tanzilu ilā al-qubbati wa-tabkī wa-tuʿaddidu ʿalayhi wa-tasqīhi al-sharāba wa-al-masālīqa bukratan wa-ʿashiyya
sentences.l: And she came to be, every day, coming to him morning and evening: she goes down to the dome, and weeps, and recounts over him, and gives him to drink the drink and the broths, morning and evening.
sentences.i: And every day thereafter, morning and evening, she went down to the dome, wept, recounted her sorrows over him, and gave him drink and broth, morning and evening.
sentences.n: الْمَسَالِيقَ, 'boiled meats, broths' (from سَلَقَ, 'to boil'), is paired loosely with تَسْقِيهِ, 'gives him to drink' — a verb of drinking stretched to cover food as well, in this prose's usual loose way.

sentences.t: وَ لَمْ تَزَلْ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ إِلَى ثَانِي سَنَةٍ وَ أَنَا أُطَوِّلُ رُوحِي عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lam tazal ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli ilā thānī sanatin wa-anā uṭawwilu rūḥī ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And she did not cease upon this state until a second year, and I — I lengthen my soul upon her.
sentences.i: And she went on so until a second year had passed, and all the while I bore with her patiently.
sentences.n: أُطَوِّلُ رُوحِي عَلَيْهَا, literally 'I lengthen my soul upon her', is the idiom for exercising patience, long-suffering toward someone.

sentences.t: وَ لَا الْتَفَتُّ إِلَيْهَا إِلَى يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ دَخَلْتُ عَلَيْهَا عَلَى غَفْلَةٍ مِنْهَا فَوَجَدْتُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lā iltafattu ilayhā ilā yawmin mina al-ayyāmi dakhaltu ʿalayhā ʿalā ghaflatin minhā fa-wajadtuhā
sentences.l: and I did not turn my attention to her, until one day of the days I went in to her by surprise, unnoticed by her, and I found her
sentences.i: and paid her no heed — until one day I came upon her unannounced, without her knowing, and found her

sentences.t: تَبْكِي وَ تَقُولُ لَمَّا تَغَيَّبْتَ عَنْ نَاظِرِي يَا نُزْهَةَ خَاطِرِي حَدِّثْنِي يَا رُوحِي كَلِّمْنِي يَا حَبِيبِي وَ أَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: tabkī wa-taqūlu lammā taghayyabta ʿan nāẓirī yā nuzhata khāṭirī ḥaddithnī yā rūḥī kallimnī yā ḥabībī wa-anshadat taqūlu shiʿr
sentences.l: weeping and saying: Since you vanished from my sight, O delight of my mind, speak to me, O my soul, talk to me, O my beloved! And she recited, saying, in verse:
sentences.i: weeping and saying: Since you vanished from my sight, O delight of my heart, speak to me, my soul, talk to me, my beloved! And she broke into verse, reciting:

sentences.t:
عَلِمْتُ اصْطِبَارِي فِي الْهَوَى انْ سَلَوْتُمُ * فُؤَادِي وَقَلْبِي لَا يُحِبُّ سِوَاكُمُ
خَلُّوا عَظْمِي وَالرُّوحَ اَيْنَ سَرَيْتُمُ * وَاَيْنَ حَلَلْتُمُ فَادْفِنُونِي حِذَاكُمُ
وَنَادَوْا بِاسْمِي عِنْدَ قَبْرِي بِحَبِيبِكُمْ * أَنِينَ عِظَامِي عِنْدَ اصْغَا صَدَاكُمُ
sentences.tr:
ʿalimtu iṣṭibārī fī al-hawā in salawtumu * fuʾādī wa-qalbī lā yuḥibbu siwākumu
khallū ʿaẓmī wa-al-rūḥa ayna saraytumu * wa-ayna ḥalaltumu fa-idfinūnī ḥidhākumu
wa-nādaw bi-ismī ʿinda qabrī bi-ḥabībikum * anīna ʿiẓāmī ʿinda iṣghā ṣadākumu
sentences.l:
I have learned my endurance in passion, should you forget — my heart and my heart love none other than you.
Leave my bone and my soul, wherever by night you journeyed — and wherever you alighted, then bury me beside you.
And call out my name at my grave, 'by your beloved!' — the moaning of my bones, at the hearkening to your echo.
sentences.i:
I have learned to bear this passion, though you should forget me; my heart, my very soul, loves none but you.
Let my bones and my spirit go with you, wherever by night you journey, and wherever you make your home — then lay me to rest at your side.
Call out my name at my grave, and swear it by your beloved — and you will hear my very bones groan at the sound of your echo.
sentences.n: اِصْطِبَارِي and فَادْفِنُونِي carry the un-marked hamzat al-waṣl of their forms (VIII and I imperative) rather than a true hamza, so no hamza sign is added. فُؤَادِي and أَنِينَ are printed with the seated hamza (ؤ, أ) in the edition itself and are kept precomposed here, unlike the bare-alif hamzas supplied elsewhere in this night. إِصْغَا is the edition's defective spelling of إِصْغَاء, 'a hearkening, an attending-of-the-ear' — read here as a verbal noun after عِنْدَ ('at the hearkening to your echo'), though the compressed syntax of the whole line asks the reader to supply 'you will hear' before 'the moaning of my bones.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَتْ وَ هِيَ تَبْكِي
sentences.tr: thumma anshadat wa hiya tabkī
sentences.l: Then she recited, and she [was] weeping
sentences.i: Then she recited, weeping.

sentences.t:
فَيَوْمُ الْاَمَانِي يَوْمُ فَوْزِي بِقُرْبِكُمْ * وَيَوْمُ الْمَنَايَا يَوْمُ اِعْرَاضِكُمْ عَنِّي
اِذَا بِتُّ مُسْرِعًا اَشُدُّ بِالسُّرَى * مُوصِلَكُمْ عِنْدِي اِلَى الْاَمَنِ
sentences.tr:
fa-yawmu al-amānī yawmu fawzī bi-qurbikum * wa-yawmu al-manāyā yawmu iʿrāḍikum ʿannī
idhā bittu musriʿan ashuddu bi-al-surā * mūṣilakum ʿindī ilā al-amani
sentences.l: The day of hopes is the day of my triumph in your nearness, and the day of deaths is the day of your turning-away from me; when I pass the night hastening, binding myself to the night-journey * that brings you, in my reckoning, to safety
sentences.i: The day of my hopes is the day I win your nearness, and the day of death is the day you turn from me; when I lie awake, hurrying through the night's journey, it is you I carry, in my own heart, safely home.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُلْتُ وَأَنْشَدْتُ
sentences.tr: thumma qultu wa-anshadtu
sentences.l: Then I said, and recited:

sentences.t:
لَوْ أَنَّنِي أَحْبَبْتُ فِي كُلِّ نِعْمَة۟ * وَكَانَتْ لِيَ الدُّنْيَا وَمُلْكُ الْاَكَاسِرَه۟
لَمَا سَوَّيْتُ عِنْدِي جَنَاحَ بَعُوضَة۟ * اِذَا لَمْ تَكُنْ عَيْنِي لِشَخْصِكَ نَاظِرَه۟
sentences.tr:
law annanī aḥbabtu fī kulli niʿmah * wa-kānat liya al-dunyā wa-mulku al-akāsirah
lamā sawwaytu ʿindī janāḥa baʿūḍah * idhā lam takun ʿaynī li-shakhṣika nāẓirah
sentences.l: If I loved truly in every blessing, and the world were mine, and the kingship of the Chosroes — I would not have equaled, in my reckoning, a gnat's-wing, if my eye were not, for your form, a gazer
sentences.i: Had I loved through every blessing, with the world mine, and the dominion of the Chosroe kings besides, I would not have valued it at a gnat's wing, were my eye not fixed in gazing upon your form.

sentences.t: قَالَ صَاحِبُ الْحَدِيثِ
sentences.tr: qāla ṣāḥibu al-ḥadīthi
sentences.l: The teller of the account said:

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ كَلَامِهَا وَبُكَاءِهَا قُلْتُ لَهَا يَا بِنْتَ عَمِّي يَكْفِيكِي مِنَ الْحُزْنِ فَمَا يُغْنِيكِي مِنَ الْبُكَاءِ مَا بَقِيَ يَنْفَعُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min kalāmihā wa-bukāʾihā qultu lahā yā binta ʿammī yakfīki min al-ḥuzni fa-mā yughnīki min al-bukāʾi mā baqiya yanfaʿu
sentences.l: So when she had finished her speech and her weeping, I said to her: O daughter of my uncle, let grief be enough for you; for weeping does not avail you — what remains [of it] is no benefit.
sentences.i: So when she had finished her speaking and her weeping, I said to her, 'O daughter of my uncle, let grief be enough for you; weeping will do you no good — nothing more is to be gained by it.'
sentences.n: The archive spells the 2nd-person feminine object suffix with an extra ي (يكفيكي، يغنيكي rather than يكفيكِ، يغنيكِ) — a Middle Arabic spelling of the pronoun -ki that recurs in this text; read simply as '-you' (fem.).

sentences.t: قَالَتْ
sentences.tr: qālat
sentences.l: She said:

sentences.t: لَا تَتَعَرَّضْ لِي فِيمَا أَعْمَلُهُ وَإِنِ اِعْتَرَضْتِ لِي قَتَلْتُ نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: lā tataʿarraḍ lī fīmā aʿmaluhu wa-ini iʿtaraḍti lī qataltu nafsī
sentences.l: Do not interfere with me in what I do; and if you interfere with me, I will kill myself.
sentences.i: Do not meddle in what I do; and if you cross me, I will kill myself.
sentences.n: تتعرض keeps the plain form without the expected feminine ـي ending, though the wife is addressed — a leveling of 2nd-person feminine verb endings that recurs through this text's Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: فَسَكَتْتُ عَنْهَا وَسَلَّمْتُ إِلَيْهَا حَالَهَا فَلَمْ تَزَلْ فِي حُزْنٍ وَبُكَاءٍ وَتَعْدِيدِ سَنَةٍ أُخْرَى
sentences.tr: fa-sakattu ʿanhā wa-sallamtu ilayhā ḥālahā fa-lam tazal fī ḥuznin wa-bukāʾin wa-taʿdīdi sanatin ukhrā
sentences.l: So I fell silent about her, and I handed her situation over to her; and she did not cease [to be] in grief and weeping and the counting of another year.
sentences.i: So I said no more to her and left the matter to her; and she continued in grief and weeping, marking off another year.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ السَّنَةِ الثَّالِثَةِ دَخَلْتُ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ وَأَنَا مُغْتَاظٌ لِحَادِثٍ عَرَضَ لِي وَقَدْ طَالَ بِي هَذَا الْعَنَاءُ الشَّدِيدُ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda al-sanati al-thālithati dakhaltu yawman min al-ayyāmi wa-anā mughtāẓun li-ḥādithin ʿaraḍa lī wa-qad ṭāla bī hādhā al-ʿanāʾu al-shadīdu
sentences.l: And after the third year, I entered one day of the days, while I [was] enraged over an incident [that] had befallen me, and this severe distress had already grown long upon me,
sentences.i: And after the third year had passed, I went in one day, angered over some matter that had come up, this harsh distress having worn on me so long,

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُهَا نَحْوَ الضَّرِيحِ دَاخِلَ الْقُبَّةِ وَهِيَ تَقُولُ يَا سَيِّدِي لَا أَسْمَعُ مِنْكَ وَلَا كَلِمَةً وَاحِدَةً
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtuhā naḥwa al-ḍarīḥi dākhila al-qubbati wa-hiya taqūlu yā sayyidī lā asmaʿu minka wa-lā kalimatan wāḥidatan
sentences.l: And I found her near the tomb, inside the dome, while she was saying: 'O my master, I do not hear from you, not even a single word,
sentences.i: And I found her by the tomb, inside the dome, saying, 'O my master, I hear from you not even a single word,

sentences.t: يَا سَيِّدِي لَهَا لَا تَرُدُّ عَلَيَّ جَوَابًا
sentences.tr: yā sayyidī lahā lā taruddu ʿalayya jawāban
sentences.l: O my master — to her(?), you do not return to me an answer
sentences.i: O my master, you give me no answer back.
sentences.n: The word لها ('to/for her') sits oddly in this clause; the line may be corrupt or a scribal slip. The translation follows the wife's continued address to the tomb.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma anshadat taqūlu
sentences.l: Then she recited, saying:

sentences.t:
يَا قَبْرُ يَا قَبْرُ هَلْ زَالَتْ مَحَاسِنُه۟ * اَمْ زَالَ مِنْكَ ضِيَاكَ الْمَنْظَرُ النَّضِرُ
يَا قَبْرُ مَا اَنْتَ لِي اَرْضٌ وَلَا فَلَكٌ * فَلَيْفَ يَجْمَعُ فِيكَ الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ
sentences.tr:
yā qabru yā qabru hal zālat maḥāsinuh * am zāla minka ḍiyāka al-manẓaru al-naḍiru
yā qabru mā anta lī arḍun wa-lā falakun * fa-layfa yajmaʿu fīka al-shamsu wa-al-qamaru
sentences.l: O tomb, O tomb, have its charms departed, or has there departed from you your gleam, the fresh sight? / O tomb, you are to me neither earth nor a heavenly sphere; so how do the sun and the moon gather in you?
sentences.i: O tomb, O tomb, have its beauties faded, or has your brightness left you — that fresh, blooming sight? / O tomb, to me you are neither earth nor heaven's sphere — how then do the sun and the moon come together within you?
sentences.n: The archive prints فليف where فكيف ('so how') is plainly meant — likely a printing slip (ل for ك). Vocalized and translated here as the sense requires.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَهَا وَشِعْرَهَا اِزْدَدْتُ غَيْظًا عَلَى غَيْظِى وَقُلْتُ أَوَّاهْ إِلَى كَمْ ذَا الْحُزْنِ وَأَنْشَدْتُ أَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāmahā wa-shiʿrahā izdadtu ghayẓan ʿalā ghayẓī wa-qultu awwāh ilā kam dhā al-ḥuzni wa-anshadtu aqūlu
sentences.l: So when I heard her speech and her verse, I increased in wrath upon my wrath, and I said: 'Alas — how much longer, this grief?' And I recited, saying:
sentences.i: When I heard her words and her verse, my fury grew upon fury, and I said, 'Enough! How much longer must this grief go on?' And I recited, saying:

sentences.t:
يَا قَبْرُ يَا قَبْرُ هَلْ زَالَتْ مَسَاخِمُه۟ * اَمْ زَالَ مِنْكَ ضِيَاكَ الْمَنْظَرُ الْقَدَرُ
يَا قَبْرُ مَا اَنْتَ لَا حَوْضٌ وَلَا قَدَرٌ * فَكَيْفَ يَجْمَعُ فِيكَ النَّجْمُ وَالْكَدَرُ
sentences.tr:
yā qabru yā qabru hal zālat masākhimuh * am zāla minka ḍiyāka al-manẓaru al-qadaru
yā qabru mā anta lā ḥawḍun wa-lā qadarun * fa-kayfa yajmaʿu fīka al-najmu wa-al-kadaru
sentences.l: O tomb, O tomb, have its blacknesses departed, or has there departed from you your gleam, the sooty sight? / O tomb, you are not a basin, nor a cooking-pot; so how do the star and the murk gather in you?
sentences.i: O tomb, O tomb, has its blackness faded, or has your glimmer left you — that sooty sight? / O tomb, you are neither a basin nor a pot — how then do the star and the gloom come together within you?
sentences.n: The husband's verse mimics and mocks the wife's: her 'beauties'/'fresh' (محاسن / نضر) become 'blacknesses'/'sooty' (مساخم / قدر) — a jab at the dead man's color — and her earth-and-sphere, sun-and-moon are downgraded to a basin, a cooking-pot, and mere murk (قدر plays on قِدْر, 'cooking-pot').

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامِي وَثَبَتْ قَائِمَةً وَقَالَتْ وَيْلَكَ يَا كَلْبُ أَنْتَ الَّذِي فَعَلْتَ مَعِي هَذَا الْفِعْلَ وَ جَرَحَتْ مَعْشُوقَ قَلْبِي وَ أَوْجَعَتْنِي وَ شَبَابُهُ وَ لَهُ ثَلٰثُ سِنِينَ لَا هُوَ مَيِّتٌ وَ لَا هُوَ حَيٌّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmī wa-thabatat qāʾimatan wa-qālat waylaka yā kalb anta alladhī faʿalta maʿī hādhā al-fiʿl wa-jaraḥat maʿshūqa qalbī wa-awjaʿatnī wa-shabābuhu wa-lahu thalāthu sinīna lā huwa mayyitun wa-lā huwa ḥayyun
sentences.l: So when she heard my words, she sprang up standing, and said: Woe to you, o dog! You are the one-who did this deed to me, and wounded the beloved of my heart, and pained me — and his youth: he has [had] three years, neither dead nor alive.
sentences.i: So when she heard my words, she sprang to her feet and cried: Woe to you, dog! It is you who did this to me — who wounded the beloved of my heart and brought me such pain — and for three years now his youth has been neither dead nor alive!
sentences.n: The Arabic strings its clauses loosely with 'and' rather than subordinating them; 'his youth' stands in loose apposition to 'the beloved of my heart', both referring to the same wounded slave-lover. This paratactic style recurs through the passage.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا يَا أَفْنَرَ الْقَحْبَاتِ وَ أَوْسَخُ الْمَنْيُوكَاتِ الْعَشَّاقَاتِ الْعَبِيدِ الْمَبَرْطَلَاتِ نَعَمْ أَنَا فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā yā afnara al-qaḥbāt wa-awsakhu al-manyūkāt al-ʿashshāqāt al-ʿabīd al-mabarṭalāt naʿam anā faʿaltu dhālika
sentences.l: Then I said to her: O most-depraved of-the-whores, and filthiest of-the-fucked-women, lovers of-the-slaves, the-bribed-ones — yes, I did that.
sentences.i: Then I said to her: You depraved whore of whores, you filthy slut who screws slaves for bribes — yes, I did it!
sentences.n: The rasm reads afnar, which yields no known root; the sense and the rhythm of this string of insults point to afjar, elative of fajara ('to be wanton/depraved'), and it is rendered that way here, though the archive's own letters (a-f-n-r) are kept in the vocalisation. The insults themselves — 'whores', 'the fucked-ones', 'lovers of slaves', 'the bribed-ones' (procuresses) — are coarse and vulgar in the Arabic and are rendered with equivalent force rather than softened.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنّي أَخَذْتُ سَيْفِي وَ جَرْدَتُهُ فِي كَفِّي وَ صَوَّبَتُ عَلَيْهَا لِأَقْتُلَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma innī akhadhtu sayfī wa-jaradtuhu fī kaffī wa-ṣawwabtu ʿalayhā li-aqtulahā
sentences.l: Then, verily-I took my sword, and bared it in my palm, and aimed [it] at her, to kill her.
sentences.i: Then I took my sword, drew it bare in my hand, and leveled it at her, to kill her.
sentences.n: 'thumma innī' ('then, indeed I...') is a stock narrative hinge in the Nights — loosely just 'and then'; it recurs through this passage as 'thumma innahā' / 'thumma inna' ('then she...' / 'then indeed...').

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامِي وَ رَأَتْنِي مُصَمِّمًا عَلَى قَتْلِهَا ضَحِكَتْ وَ قَالَتْ تَخْسَأْ يَا كَلْبُ هَيْهَاتَ أَنْ يَرْجِعُ مَا فَاتَ أَوْ تَجِيءُ الْأَمْواتُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmī wa-raʾatnī muṣamimman ʿalā qatlihā ḍaḥikat wa-qālat takhsaʾ yā kalb hayhāta an yarjiʿa mā fāta aw tajīʾa al-amwāt
sentences.l: So when she heard my words, and saw me resolved upon killing her, she laughed, and said: Be-despised, o dog! Far be it that what has passed should return, or the dead should come.
sentences.i: But when she heard my words and saw that I was resolved to kill her, she only laughed and said: Begone, you dog! It is not likely that what is past should return, or that the dead should come back to life.
sentences.n: takhsaʾ echoes the curse used to drive off a dog (khasaʾa), fitting the insult 'yā kalb' that follows it. hayhāta is a fixed exclamation of impossibility, 'how far-fetched!'.

sentences.t: لَقَدْ أَمْكَنَنِي اللّٰهُ بِمَنْ فَعَلَ بِي هَذَا وَ كَانَتْ فِي قَلْبِي مِنْهُ نَارٌ لَا تُطْفَى وَ لَهِيبٌ لَا
sentences.tr: laqad amkananī Allāhu bi-man faʿala bī hādhā wa-kānat fī qalbī minhu nārun lā tuṭfā wa-lahībun lā —
sentences.l: God has indeed given me power over him who did this to me; and there was in my heart, because of him, a fire not [to be] put out, and a flame not —
sentences.i: God has indeed delivered into my power the one who did this to me — for in my heart, because of him, there burned a fire that would not be put out, and a flame that would not —
sentences.n: The verb is elided at the line's end and understood repeated from 'lā tuṭfā' ('a flame [likewise unquenched]') — ordinary economy in Arabic coordination, not a gap in the text.

sentences.t: بَغْتَةً ثُمَّ وَقَفَتْ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهَا وَ تَكَلَّمَتْ بِكَلَامٍ لَا أَفْهَمُهُ وَ قَالَتْ اُخْرُجْ بِسِحْرِي نُصْفُكَ حَجَرٌ وَ نُصْفُكَ بَشَرٌ
sentences.tr: baghtatan thumma waqafat ʿalā qadamayhā wa-takallamat bi-kalāmin lā afhamuhu wa-qālat ukhruj bi-siḥrī niṣfuka ḥajarun wa-niṣfuka basharun
sentences.l: Suddenly, then she stood upon her two feet, and spoke words I did not understand, and said: Come forth by my sorcery — your half [is] stone, and your half [is] human!
sentences.i: Then, of a sudden, she rose to her feet, uttered words I could not understand, and cried: Come forth, by my sorcery! Let half of you be stone, and half of you flesh!

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنّي صِرْتُ كَمَا تَرَى وَ بَقِيتُ لَا أَقُومُ وَ لَا أَقْعُدُ وَ لَا أَنَا مَيِّتٌ وَ لَا أَنَا حَيٌّ
sentences.tr: thumma innī ṣirtu kamā tarā wa-baqītu lā aqūmu wa-lā aqʿudu wa-lā anā mayyitun wa-lā anā ḥayyun
sentences.l: Then I became as you see, and remained: I neither stand nor sit, and I am neither dead nor alive.
sentences.i: So I became as you see me now, and have remained ever since — unable to stand, unable to sit, neither dead nor alive.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا صِرْتُ هَكَذَا سَحَرَتْ الْمَدِينَةَ وَ مَا فِيهَا مِنْ الْأَسْواقِ وَ الْغِيطَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṣirtu hākadhā saḥarat al-madīnata wa-mā fīhā min al-aswāq wa-al-ghīṭān
sentences.l: So when I became thus, she enchanted the city, and what is in it of the markets and the gardens.
sentences.i: And when I had become like this, she turned her sorcery on the city as well, on all its markets and its gardens.
sentences.n: al-ghīṭān ('gardens/fields') is the Egyptian-dialect plural of ghayṭ, one of several colloquial touches in this passage.

sentences.t: وَ كَانَتْ مَدِينَتَنَا أَرْبَعَةَ صُنُوفٍ مُسْلِمِينَ وَ نَصَارى وَ يَهُودَ وَ مَجُوسَ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat madīnatunā arbaʿata ṣunūfin muslimīna wa-naṣārā wa-yahūda wa-majūsa
sentences.l: And our city was [of] four kinds: Muslims, and Christians, and Jews, and Magians.
sentences.i: Now our city was made up of four communities: Muslims, Christians, Jews, and Magians (Zoroastrians).

sentences.t: فَسَحَرَتْهُمْ سَمَكَا فَالْأَبْيضُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَ الْأَحْمَرُ الْمَجُوسُ وَ الْأَرْزَقُ النَّصَارى وَ الْأَصْفَرُ الْيَهُودُ
sentences.tr: fa-saḥarathum samakan fa-al-abyaḍu al-muslimūna wa-al-aḥmaru al-majūsu wa-al-arzaqu al-naṣārā wa-al-aṣfaru al-yahūdu
sentences.l: So she enchanted them into fish: so-the-white [are] the Muslims, and the red the Magians, and the blue the Christians, and the yellow the Jews.
sentences.i: She turned them all into fish: the white ones are the Muslims, the red the Magians, the blue the Christians, and the yellow the Jews.
sentences.n: al-arzaq (letters a-r-z-q) reverses the two middle consonants of the ordinary word for 'blue', azraq (a-z-r-q); it is vocalised and kept as the archive spells it, a likely metathesis rather than an error to silently fix.

sentences.t: وَ سَحَرَتْ الْجَزَائرَ الْأَرْبَعَ جَبَالً مُحِيطَةً بَالْبِرْكَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-saḥarat al-jazāʾira al-arbaʿa jibālan muḥīṭatan bi-al-birka
sentences.l: And she enchanted the four islands [into] mountains surrounding the pool.
sentences.i: And the four islands she turned into mountains ringing the pool.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنّهَا كُلَّ يَومٍ تَضْرِبُنِي وَ تُعَذِّبُنِي بِالسَّوْطِ مِائْةً ضَربَةً حَتّى يَسِيلُ دَمِي وَ تَنْهَرِي أَكْتَافِي
sentences.tr: thumma innahā kulla yawmin taḍribunī wa-tuʿadhdhibunī bi-al-sawṭi miʾatan ḍarbatan ḥattā yasīlu damī wa-tanharī aktāfī
sentences.l: Then she, every day, beats me and tortures me with the whip, a hundred blows, until my blood flows and my shoulders — stream.
sentences.i: Then, every day, she beats me and tortures me with the whip — a hundred lashes — until my blood runs and my shoulders are riven and streaming.
sentences.n: tanharī is an irregular form: as printed it cannot be cleanly parsed as a standard verb. It is vocalised here preserving the archive's five letters, and rendered by sense, connecting it to nahr ('river, channel') — the shoulders 'run' or are furrowed with blood, an image of whip-scarred flesh cut like channels. Read with real caution.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تُلْبِسُنِي ثَوبَ شَعَرٍ صِفَةَ اللِّبَاسِ عَلَى نِصْفِي الْفَوْقَانِي وَ تُلْبِسُنِي هَذِهِ الثِّيابَ الْفَاخِرَةَ مِنْ فَوْقُ
sentences.tr: thumma tulbisunī thawba shaʿrin ṣifata al-libāsi ʿalā niṣfī al-fawqānī wa-tulbisunī hādhihi al-thiyāba al-fākhirata min fawqu
sentences.l: Then she clothes me [in] a garment of hair, in the fashion of clothing, over my upper half; and she clothes me [in] these fine garments from above.
sentences.i: Then she dresses me in a garment of hair, after the fashion of clothing, over my upper body — and over that she puts these splendid robes.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الشَّابَ بَكَى وَ أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-shābba bakā wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: Then indeed the young man wept, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: Then the young man wept, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: 'thumma inna...' is the Nights' classic formula for moving the story on — 'then, indeed...', here simply 'then'.

sentences.t:
صَبْرًا لِحُكْمِكَ يَا اِلٰهِي وَالْقَضَا * اَنَا صَابِرٌ اِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ لَكَ الرِّضَا
جَارُوا عَلَيْنَا وَاعْتَدَوْا وَتَجَبَّرُوا * فَلَعَلَّنِي الْفِرْدَوْسَ اَنْ نَتَعَوَّضَا
قَلْ ضِقْتُ بِالْاَمْرِ الَّذِي قَلْ نَالَنِي * فَوَسِيلَتِي بِالْمُصْطَفَى وَالْمُرْتَضَى
sentences.tr:
ṣabran li-ḥukmika yā ilāhī wa-al-qaḍā * anā ṣābirun in kāna fīhi laka al-riḍā
jārū ʿalaynā wa-iʿtadaw wa-tajabbarū * fa-laʿallanī al-firdawsa an nataʿawwaḍā
qalla ḍiqtu bi-al-amri alladhī qalla nālanī * fa-wasīlatī bi-al-Muṣṭafā wa-al-Murtaḍā
sentences.l:
Patience for your judgment, o my God, and the decree — * I am patient, if in it is your good-pleasure.
They wronged us, and transgressed, and were tyrannical — * so perhaps-I [shall win] Paradise, that we be recompensed.
Rarely have-I-been straitened by the matter which rarely befell-me — * so my recourse [is] by the Chosen-one and the Well-pleasing-one.
sentences.i:
Patience, for your judgment, O my God, and for your decree — I am content, if in it lies your good pleasure.
They have wronged us, and transgressed against us, and dealt tyrannically — perhaps Paradise shall yet be my reward.
Never have I been so pressed by a trial that so rarely comes to anyone — yet my recourse is through the Chosen One and the Well-Pleasing One.
sentences.n: al-Firdaws is the highest garden of Paradise. al-Muṣṭafā ('the Chosen One') and al-Murtaḍā ('the Well-Pleasing/Approved One') are honorific epithets — traditionally for the Prophet Muhammad and for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib respectively — invoked here as intercessors. The word printed 'قل' (qal) in the third line is vocalised here as qalla ('it became little/rare'), read idiomatically as 'rarely, seldom' — not as a defective spelling of qāla ('he said'), which does not fit the sense of the line.

sentences.t: أَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: anshadat taqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: She recited, saying these verses.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ اِلْتَفَتَ الْمَلِكُ إِلَى الشَّابِّ وَقَالَ
sentences.tr: qāla: fa-ʿinda dhālika iltafata al-maliku ilā al-shābbi wa-qāla
sentences.l: He said: Then at that, the king turned to the young man and said:

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الشَّابُّ زِدْتَنِي هَمًّا عَلَى هَمِّي بَعْدَ أَنْ فَرَّجْتَ عَنِّي غَمِّي
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-shābbu zidtanī hamman ʿalā hammī baʿda an farrajta ʿannī ghammī
sentences.l: O young man, you have added for me a worry upon my worry, after you relieved from me my anguish.
sentences.i: O young man, you have given me one worry on top of another — and this after you had relieved my distress!

sentences.t: وَلَٰكِنْ يَا فَتَى أَيْنَ هِيَ وَ أَيْنَ الْمَكَانُ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْعَبْدُ الْمَجْرُوحُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin yā fatā ayna hiya wa-ayna al-makānu alladhī fīhi al-ʿabdu al-majrūḥu
sentences.l: But, O young man, where is she, and where is the place in which is the wounded slave?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّابُّ إِنَّ الْعَبْدَ فِي الْقُبَّةِ فِي مَدْفَنِهِ رَاقِدٌ وَهِيَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَجْلِسِ الَّذِي بِحَاذِي الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shābbu: inna al-ʿabda fī al-qubbati fī madfanihi rāqidun, wa-hiya fī dhālika al-majlisi alladhī bi-ḥādhī al-bābi
sentences.l: The young man said: The slave is in the dome, lying in his burial-place, and she is in that chamber which is opposite the door.
sentences.i: The young man replied, ‘The slave lies in the dome, in his tomb, and she is in the chamber facing the door.’
sentences.n: بِحَاذِي, 'facing, opposite' (from حَاذَى, 'to be alongside'), is a Middle Arabic prepositional use where Classical prose would have بِحِذَاءِ; both carry the same sense, 'opposite, next to.'

sentences.t: تِجِي مَرَّةً فِي كُلِّ يَومٍ عِنْدَ مَا تَطْلُعُ الشَّمْسُ
sentences.tr: tijī marratan fī kulli yawmin ʿinda mā taṭluʿu al-shamsu
sentences.l: She comes once every day, when the sun rises.
sentences.n: تِجِي is the colloquial present tense of 'to come' (Classical تَجِيءُ, from جاء/يجيء), used here instead of the Classical form; a recurring feature of the narrator's Middle Arabic, not an error, and kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَأَوَّلُ مَا تِجِي تَانِي إِلَيَّ وَتُجَرِّدُنِي مِنْ أَثْوَابِي وَتَضْرِبُنِي بِالسَّوْطِ مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-awwalu mā tijī tānī ilayya wa-tujarridunī min athwābī wa-taḍribunī bi-al-sawṭi miʾata jaldatin
sentences.l: So the first thing, when she comes — next, to me — she strips me of my garments and beats me with the whip a hundred lashes.
sentences.i: The first thing she does when she arrives is come straight to me: she strips off my clothes and whips me a hundred lashes.
sentences.n: تَانِي, literally 'second' (colloquial for ثَانِي), functions here as a sequencer, 'next, then'; its precise force is not fully certain, and it may instead reflect a scribal repetition of تِجِي. Vocalized as printed.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَبْكِي وَأَصِيحُ وَلَا لِي حَرَكَةٌ أَدْفَعُهَا عَنْ نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: wa-anā abkī wa-aṣīḥu wa-lā lī ḥarakatun adfaʿuhā ʿan nafsī
sentences.l: And I weep and cry out, and I have no movement with which I might fend it off from myself.
sentences.i: And I weep and cry out, powerless to move and defend myself.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ أَنْ تُعَانِبُنِي تَنْزِلُ لِلْعَبْدِ بِالشَّرَابِ وَالْمَسْلُوقَةِ تَسْقِيهِ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda an tuʿānibunī tanzilu li-al-ʿabdi bi-al-sharābi wa-al-maslūqati tasqīhi
sentences.l: Then, after she embraces me, she goes down to the slave with the drink and the broth, to give him to drink.
sentences.i: Then, once she has embraced me, she goes down to feed and water the slave.
sentences.n: تُعَانِبُنِي as printed has no clear sense from an attested root; it is very possibly a copyist's variant of تُعَانِقُنِي, 'she embraces me' (ب and ق are easily confused in print), which fits the scene's alternation between cruelty and affection. Vocalized as printed, with this candidate reading noted.

sentences.t: وَغَدًا مِنْ بَاكِرٍ تِجِي
sentences.tr: wa-ghadan min bākirin tijī
sentences.l: And on the morrow, early, she comes.
sentences.i: And early the next morning, she comes again.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْمَلِكُ وَاللَّهِ يَا فَتَى لَأَفْعَلَنَّ مَعَكَ مَعْرُوفًا أُذْكَرُ بِهِ وَ يُؤَرِّخُونَهُ إِلَى آخِرِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: qāla al-maliku: wa-allāhi yā fatā la-afʿalanna maʿaka maʿrūfan udhkaru bihi wa-yuʾarrikhūnahu ilā ākhiri al-zamāni
sentences.l: The king said: By God, O young man, I will surely do with you a kindness by which I am remembered, and which they will chronicle until the end of time.
sentences.i: The king said, ‘By God, young man, I will surely do you a kindness for which I shall be remembered, and which will be recorded in history until the end of time.’

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْمَلِكُ يَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَهُ إِلَى أَنْ أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ وَنَامَا
sentences.tr: thumma jalasa al-maliku yataḥaddathu maʿahu ilā an aqbala al-laylu wa-nāmā
sentences.l: Then the king sat conversing with him until night came on, and the two of them slept.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ الْمَلِكُ فِي وَقْتِ السَّحَرِ وَتَجَرَّدَ مِنْ أَثْوَابِهِ وَسَلَّ سَيْفَهُ وَنَهَضَ إِلَى الْمَحَلِّ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْعَبْدُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma al-maliku fī waqti al-saḥari wa-tajarrada min athwābihi wa-salla sayfahu wa-nahaḍa ilā al-maḥalli alladhī fīhi al-ʿabdu
sentences.l: Then the king rose at the time of the last watch of the night, and stripped off his garments, and drew his sword, and got up toward the place in which the slave was.
sentences.i: Then, in the hour before dawn, the king rose, stripped off his clothes, drew his sword, and made his way to where the slave lay.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ إِلَى الشَّمْعِ وَالْقَنَادِيلِ وَبَخُورَاتٍ وَأَدْهَانٍ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ilā al-shamʿi wa-al-qanādīli wa-bakhūrātin wa-adhānin
sentences.l: And he looked at the candles, and the lamps, and incense, and oils.

sentences.t: وَسَارَ يَقْصِدُ الْعَبْدَ حَتّى أَتَاهُ وَضَرَبَهُ ضَرْبَةً فَقَتَلَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-sāra yaqṣidu al-ʿabda ḥattā atāhu wa-ḍarabahu ḍarbatan fa-qatalahu
sentences.l: And he went, making for the slave, until he reached him, and struck him a blow, and killed him.
sentences.i: And he went straight for the slave, and when he reached him, struck him down with a single blow.

sentences.t: وَحَمَلَهُ عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ وَرَمَاهُ فِي بِئْرٍ كَانَتْ فِي الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamalahu ʿalā ẓahrihi wa-ramāhu fī biʾrin kānat fī al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And he carried him on his back, and threw him into a well that was in the palace.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَزَلَ وَالْتَفَّ بِأَثْوَابِ الْعَبْدِ وَرَقَدَ دَاخِلَ الضَّرِيحِ وَ السَّيْفُ مَعَهُ مَسْلُولٌ فِي طُولِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma nazala wa-iltaffa bi-athwābi al-ʿabdi wa-raqada dākhila al-ḍarīḥi wa-al-sayfu maʿahu maslūlun fī ṭūlihi
sentences.l: Then he went down, and wrapped himself in the slave's garments, and lay down inside the tomb, with the sword beside him, drawn, along its length.
sentences.i: Then he went down, wrapped himself in the slave's clothes, and lay down inside the tomb, his drawn sword beside him along his body.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ أَتَتْ الْمَلْعُونَةُ السَّاحِرَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda sāʿatin atati al-malʿūnatu al-sāḥiratu
sentences.l: Then after an hour, the accursed sorceress came.

sentences.t: فَأَوَّلُ مَا دَخَلَتْ جَرَّدَتْ اِبْنَ عَمِّهَا مِنْ ثِيَابِهِ وَأَخَذَتْ سَوْطًا وَضَرَبَتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-awwalu mā dakhalat jarradati ibna ʿammihā min thiyābihi wa-akhadhat sawṭan wa-ḍarabathu
sentences.l: As soon as she entered, she stripped her cousin of his clothes, and took a whip, and beat him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَوَّاهُ يَكْفِينِي مَا أَنَا فِيهِ يَا بِنْتَ عَمِّي اِرْحَمِينِي يَا بِنْتَ عَمِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla: āwāhu yakfīnī mā anā fīhi yā binta ʿammī irḥamīnī yā binta ʿammī
sentences.l: And he said: Ah! Enough for me is what I am in — O daughter of my uncle, have mercy on me, O daughter of my uncle!
sentences.i: He cried out, ‘Ah, enough of what I suffer! O my cousin, have mercy on me, O my cousin!’

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ كُنْتَ أَنْتَ رَحِمْتَنِي وَأَبْقَيْتَ لِي مَعْشُوقِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat: kunta anta raḥimtanī wa-abqayta lī maʿshūqī
sentences.l: And she said: Was it you who showed me mercy, and left me my beloved?
sentences.i: She answered, ‘Was it you who showed me mercy, and spared me my beloved?’
sentences.n: A bitter rhetorical retort: 'Was it you who showed me mercy?' — recalling that her husband's sorcery had earlier left her lover only half-destroyed rather than killed outright.

sentences.t: وَضَرَبَتْ حَتّى تَعِبَتْ وَسَالَ الدَّمُ مِنْ جُنُوبِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḍarabat ḥattā taʿibat wa-sāla al-dammu min junūbihi
sentences.l: And she beat him until she grew tired, and the blood flowed from his sides.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَلْبَسَتْهُ اللِّبَاسَ الشَّعْرَانِيَّ وَالْقُمَاشَ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma albasathu al-libāsa al-shaʿrāniyya wa-al-qumāsha min fawqihi
sentences.l: Then she dressed him in the haircloth garment, and the cloth over it.
sentences.i: Then she clothed him in a hairshirt, with fine cloth laid over it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَزَلَتْ إِلَى الْعَبْدِ وَمَعَهَا قَدَحُ الشَّرَابِ وَطَاسَةُ مَسْلُوقَةٍ وَنَزَلَتْ فِي الْقُبَّةِ
sentences.tr: thumma nazalat ilā al-ʿabdi wa-maʿahā qadaḥu al-sharābi wa-ṭāsatu maslūqatin, wa-nazalat fī al-qubbati
sentences.l: Then she went down to the slave, with her a cup of the drink and a bowl of broth, and she went down into the dome.
sentences.i: Then she went down to the slave, carrying a cup of drink and a bowl of broth, and descended into the dome.

sentences.t: وَبَكَتْ وَوَلْوَلَتْ وَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي كَلِّمْنِي يَا سَيِّدِي حَدِّثْنِي وَ
sentences.tr: wa-bakat wa-walwalat wa-qālat: yā sayyidī kallimnī, yā sayyidī ḥaddithnī, wa-
sentences.l: And she wept and wailed, and said: O my master, speak to me! O my master, tell me! and—
sentences.i: And she wept and wailed, crying, ‘O my lord, speak to me! O my lord, answer me!’—
sentences.n: The line breaks off on the bare conjunction وَ ('and'), as printed at the end of P52L22; the sorceress's lament continues directly into the verses that follow, which form their own sense unit under the verse convention.

sentences.t:
حَتّٰى مَتٰى هَذَا الصُّدُودُ وَذَا الجَفَا * أَوَمَا جَرَى مِنْ أَدْمُعِي سَيْلٌ كَفَا
فَلَكُم تُطِيلُ الهَجرَ لِي مُتَعَمِّدًا * اِن كَانَ قَصدُكَ حَاسِدِي فَقَد اِشتَفَى
sentences.tr:
ḥattā matā hādhā al-ṣudūdu wa-dhā al-jafā * awa-mā jarā min admuʿī saylun kafā
fa-lakum tuṭīlu al-hajra lī mutaʿammidan * in kāna qaṣduka ḥāsidī fa-qad ishtafā
sentences.l:
How long will this turning-away last, and this harshness? * Has not a flood flowed from my tears, enough?
How long you prolong this estrangement from me, deliberately! * If your aim was my envier — he has had his fill.
sentences.i:
How long shall this coldness endure, and this cruelty? * Has not a flood already flowed enough from my tears?
How long you draw out this parting from me, and by design! * If it was my envier you meant to gratify, he has had his fill indeed.
sentences.n: فَلَكُمْ ('to you…') does not smoothly agree in number with the singular verb تُطِيلُ that follows it; the reproach for prolonged estrangement is clear even where the grammar of the address is loose — possibly an honorific plural, possibly an artifact of the verse's transmission.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا بَكَتْ وَ قَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي كَلِّمْنِي وَ حَادِثْنِي
sentences.tr: thumma innahā bakat wa-qālat yā sayyidī kallimnī wa-ḥādithnī
sentences.l: Then she wept and said, "O my master, speak to me and talk with me."

sentences.t: وَ الْمَلِكُ خَفَّضَ صَوتَهُ وَ عَقَلَ لِسَانَهُ وَ تَكَلَّمَ بِكَلَامِ السُّودانِ وَ قَالَ أَوَّاهْ أَوَّاهْ لَا حَولَ وَ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-maliku khaffaḍa ṣawtahu wa-ʿaqala lisānahu wa-takallama bi-kalāmi al-Sūdāni wa-qāla awwāh awwāh lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīmi
sentences.l: And the king lowered his voice and bound his tongue and spoke with the speech of the Blacks, and said, "Alas, alas! There is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Great."
sentences.i: And the king lowered his voice, checked his tongue, and spoke in a feigned foreign accent, saying, "Alas, alas! There is no power nor strength save in God, the Most High, the Most Great."
sentences.n: "السودان" here is the period term for Black Africans generally, not a nation-name; the king is still playing the murdered slave and disguises his voice to match.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُ صَرَخَتْ مِنْ الْفَرَحِ وَ غُشِيَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmahu ṣarakhat min al-faraḥi wa-ghushiya ʿalayhā
sentences.l: Then when she heard his speech, she cried out from joy, and she was overcome.
sentences.i: So when she heard his voice, she cried out for joy, and fainted.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا اسْتَفَاقَتْ وَ قَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي هُوَ صَحِيحُ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā istafāqat wa-qālat yā sayyidī huwa ṣaḥīḥun
sentences.l: Then she awoke, and said, "O my master, is it true?"

sentences.t: وَ الْمَلِكُ أَضْعَفَ صَوتَهُ وَ قَالَ يَا مَلْعُونَةُ أَنْتِي تَسْتَأْهِلِي مَنْ يُكَلِّمُكِ وَ يُحَدِّثُكِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-maliku aḍʿafa ṣawtahu wa-qāla yā malʿūnatu antī tastahilī man yukallimuki wa-yuḥaddithuki
sentences.l: And the king weakened his voice further, and said, "O accursed woman, do you deserve one who speaks to you and talks with you?"
sentences.i: And the king made his voice fainter still, and said, "O accursed woman, do you deserve that anyone should speak to you, or talk with you?"
sentences.n: "تستاهلي" (for tastaḥiqqīna, "you deserve") drops the final -na of the feminine imperfect, as does "عليكي"/"انتي" adding an extra ي to the 2fs ending -ki — both recurring Middle Arabic features in this passage, flagged here and then left unremarked.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ مَا سَبَبُهُ
sentences.tr: qālat mā sababuhu
sentences.l: She said, "What is its cause?"

sentences.t: قَالَ سَبَبُهُ أَنَّكِ بِطُولِ النَّهارِ تُعَاقِبِي زَوجَكِ وَ هُوَ يَسْتَغِيثُ وَ أَحْرَمَنِي النَّومَ مِنْ الْعَشَا إِلَى الْصَبَاحِ وَ يَتَضَرَّعُ وَ يَدْعُو عَلَيَّ وَ عَلَيْكِي
sentences.tr: qāla sababuhu annaki bi-ṭūli al-nahāri tuʿāqibī zawjaki wa-huwa yastaghīthu wa-aḥramanī al-nawma min al-ʿashā ilā al-ṣabāḥi wa-yataḍarraʿu wa-yadʿū ʿalayya wa-ʿalayki
sentences.l: He said, "Its cause is that all the length of the day you torment your husband, and he cries for help, and he has deprived me of sleep from the evening until the morning, and he pleads and prays against me and against you."
sentences.i: He said, "The cause is this: all day long you torment your husband, so that he cries out for help; he has robbed me of sleep from evening until dawn, pleading and praying against the two of us."

sentences.t: وَ قَدْ أَقْلَقَنِي وَ أَضْرَّنِي وَلَولَا هَذَا لَكُنْتُ تَعَافَيتُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad aqlaqanī wa-aḍarranī wa-lawlā hādhā la-kuntu taʿāfaytu
sentences.l: And it has troubled me and harmed me, and were it not for this, I would have recovered.
sentences.i: It has troubled me and done me harm — but for this, I would already have recovered.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا الَّذِي مَنَعَنِي عَنْ جَوابِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā alladhī manaʿanī ʿan jawābiki
sentences.l: So this is what has prevented me from your answer.
sentences.i: So this is what has kept me from answering you.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ عَنْ إِذْنِكَ أُخَلِّصُهُ مِمَّا هُوَ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ʿan idhnika ukhalliṣuhu mimmā huwa fīhi
sentences.l: So she said, "With your permission, I will free him from what he is in."
sentences.i: She said, "With your leave, I will free him from his plight."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الْمَلِكُ خَلِّصِيهِ وَ رَيِّحِينَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-maliku khalliṣīhi wa-rayyiḥīnā
sentences.l: The king said to her, "Free him, and give us rest."
sentences.n: "ريحينا" (rayyiḥīnā, "give us rest") is a Form II verb doing the work Classical would give to Form IV أريحينا — one of several such substitutions in this passage.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ سَمْعًا وَ طَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qālat samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: So she said, "hearing and obedience."
sentences.i: She said, "With hearing and obedience."

sentences.t: وَ قَامَتْ وَ خَرَجَتْ مِنْ الْقُبَّةِ إِلَى الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāmat wa-kharajat min al-qubbati ilā al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And she rose and went out from the dome to the palace.

sentences.t: وَ أَخَذَتْ طَاسَةً وَ مَلَأَتْهَا مَاءًا وَ تَكَلَّمَتْ عَلَيْهَا بِكَلَامِ فَغَلَتْ الْطَّاسَةُ وَ بَقْبَقَتْ وَ صَارتْ تَغْلِي كَمَا يَغْلِي الْقِدرُ عَلَى النَّارِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhat ṭāsatan wa-malaʾathā māʾan wa-takallamat ʿalayhā bi-kalāmin fa-ghalati al-ṭāsatu wa-baqbaqat wa-ṣārat taghlī kamā yaghlī al-qidru ʿalā al-nāri
sentences.l: And she took a basin and filled it with water and spoke over it certain words, and the basin boiled and bubbled and fell to boiling as the pot boils upon the fire.
sentences.i: She took a basin, filled it with water, and spoke certain words over it, so that the basin boiled and bubbled and began to boil as a pot boils on the fire.

sentences.t: وَ طَرَشَتْهُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ṭarashathu bihā
sentences.l: And she sprinkled him with it.
sentences.n: "طرشته" ("sprinkled him") stands where رشّته would be usual; a minor lexical variant, its sense plain from context.

sentences.t: وَ قَالَتْ بِيَحَقْ مَا تَلَوتُهُ وَ قُلْتُهُ إِنْ كُنْتِ صِرْتِ هَكَذَا بِسِحْرِي وَ سُكْرِي فَاُخْرُجْ مِنْ هَذِةْ الْصُورةِ إِلَى صُورتَكَ الْأُولَى
sentences.tr: wa-qālat bi-yaḥaqq mā talawtuhu wa-qultuhu in kunti ṣirti hākadhā bi-siḥrī wa-sukrī fa-ukhruj min hādhihi al-ṣūrati ilā ṣūratika al-ūlā
sentences.l: And she said, "By the truth of what I have recited and said — if it is by my sorcery and my intoxication that you have become thus — then come out from this form to your former form."
sentences.i: And she said, "By the truth of what I have recited and spoken — since it is by my sorcery and my spell that you have become thus — come forth from this shape into your former shape!"
sentences.n: "بيحق" is an unexpected spelling for بِحَقِّ ("by the right/truth of," the usual oath formula); the intruding ي is unexplained, kept as printed. "سكري" (literally "my drunkenness") is paired with "سحري" ("my magic") for the rhyme (sajʿ); together they read as "my magic and my spell." "هذة" spells the demonstrative "this" (fem.) with ة where هذه would be expected — a spelling variant, not a different word.

sentences.t: وَ إِذَا بِالشَّابِ اِنْتَفَضَ وَ قَامَ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-shābbi intafaḍa wa-qāma ʿalā qadamayhi
sentences.l: And behold, the young man shook and stood up on his feet.
sentences.i: And suddenly the young man gave a start and rose to his feet.

sentences.t: وَ فَرِحَ بِخَلَاصِهِ وَ قَالَ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللّٰهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللّٰهِ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ سَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: wa-fariḥa bi-khalāṣihi wa-qāla ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāhu wa-ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāhi ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama
sentences.l: And he rejoiced at his deliverance, and said, "I testify that there is no god but God, and I testify that Muhammad is the messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace."

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ اُخْرُجْ وَ لَا تَرْجِعْ إِلَى هُنَا وَ إِلَّا قَتَلْتُكَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu ukhruj wa-lā tarjiʿ ilā hunā wa-illā qataltuka
sentences.l: Then she said to him, "Go out, and do not return here, or else I will kill you."
sentences.i: Then she said to him, "Go now, and never come back here, or else I will kill you."

sentences.t: وَ صَرَخَتْ فِي وَجْهِهِ فَخَرَجَ مِنْ بَينَ يَدَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ṣarakhat fī wajhihi fa-kharaja min bayna yadayhā
sentences.l: And she screamed in his face, so he went out from before her.

sentences.t: وَ عَادتْ إِلَى الْقُبَّةِ وَ نَزَلَتْ وَ قَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي اُخْرُجْ لِي حَتَّى أَنْظُرَ إِلَى صُورتَكَ الْجَمِيلَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿādat ilā al-qubbati wa-nazalat wa-qālat yā sayyidī ukhruj lī ḥattā anẓura ilā ṣūratika al-jamīlati
sentences.l: And she returned to the dome, and went down, and said, "O my master, come out to me, so that I may look upon your beautiful form."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الْمَلِكُ بِكَلَامٍ ضَعِيفٍ أَيْشْ عَمَلْتِي أَرَحْتِينِي مِنْ الْفَرْعِ وَ لَمْ تُرِيحِينِي مِنْ الْأَصْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-maliku bi-kalāmin ḍaʿīfin aysh ʿamalti araḥtīnī min al-farʿi wa-lam turīḥīnī min al-aṣli
sentences.l: The king said to her in a weak voice, "What have you done? You have given me rest from the branch, but you have not given me rest from the root."
sentences.i: The king said to her, in a faint voice, "What have you done? You have relieved me of the branch, but not of the root."
sentences.n: "ايش" is the colloquial interrogative "what" (from ayyu shayʾin, "which thing"), still current in spoken Arabic today. "The branch" and "the root" figure the young man's own curse as the surface symptom and the city's curse as its deeper cause.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا حَبِيبِي يَا سَيِّدِي مَا هُوَ الْأَحَلُّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā ḥabībī yā sayyidī mā huwa al-aḥall
sentences.l: So she said, "O my beloved, O my master, what is the root?"
sentences.i: She said, "O my beloved, O my master — what is it, then?"
sentences.n: The archive prints "الاحل" here (with ح), where the king's own word the line before was spelled "الاصل" (with ص, "the root"); the two letters are easily confused in this typeface, and context makes it near-certain she is echoing his word rather than asking about "الأحلّ" ("the most lawful thing"). Kept as printed; this reading is offered as the likely one, not a certainty.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَبَلَا لَكِ يَا مَلْعُونَةُ أَهْلُ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَ الْأَرْبَعِ جَزَائِرِ
sentences.tr: qāla wa-balā laki yā malʿūnatu ahlu hādhihi al-madīnati wa-al-arbaʿi jazāʾiri
sentences.l: He said, "Woe to you, O accursed woman: the people of this city, and of the four islands —"
sentences.i: He said, "Woe to you, accursed woman! The people of this city, and of the four islands…"
sentences.n: "وبلا" appears to stand for وَيْلًا (the curse formula "وَيْلًا لَكِ", "woe to you"), with ب printed for ي; kept as printed. The sense fits the king's continuing curse, "يا ملعونة."

sentences.t: كُلَّ لَيلَةٍ إِذَا اِنْتَصَفَ اللَّيلُ تَشِيلُ الْسَمَكُ رُؤُسَهَا وَ تَسْغِيثُ وَ تَدْعُوا عَلَيَّ وَ عَلَيْلِي فَهُوَ سَبَبُ مَنْعِ عَافِيتِي
sentences.tr: kulla laylatin idhā intaṣafa al-laylu tashīlu al-samaku ruʾūsahā wa-tastaghīthu wa-tadʿū ʿalayya wa-ʿalayki fa-huwa sababu manʿi ʿāfiyatī
sentences.l: every night, when the night reaches its middle, the fish raise their heads and cry for help and pray against me and against you, and that is the cause of the withholding of my health.
sentences.i: Every night, at the stroke of midnight, the fish lift up their heads and cry out for help, praying against the two of us — and that is what withholds my recovery.
sentences.n: "تسغيث" prints without the ت of the pattern تستغيث ("cries for help") — a dropped letter, read here as tastaghīthu. "عليلي" most likely stands for عليكي ("against you"), echoing the same phrase used earlier (ل for ك); both kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَرُوحِي خَلِّصِيهُمْ عَاجِلًا وَ نُعَانِي
sentences.tr: fa-rūḥī khalliṣīhim ʿājilan wa-nuʿānī
sentences.l: So go, free them quickly, for we suffer.
sentences.i: Go now, free them at once — for we suffer for it.
sentences.n: "روحي" is the colloquial imperative "go!" (from rāḥa/yarūḥu), standing where Classical would use اذهبي.

sentences.t: خُذِي بِيدِي وَ أَقِيمِينِي
sentences.tr: khudhī bi-yadī wa-aqīmīnī
sentences.l: Take me by my hand and set me upright.
sentences.i: Take my hand, and raise me up.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ تَوَجَّهَتْ لِي الْعَافِيةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qad tawajjahat liya al-ʿāfiyatu
sentences.l: For wellness has now turned toward me.
sentences.i: For my health has come back to me at last.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَ الْمَلِكِ وَهِي نَظُنُّهُ الْعَبْدَ وَهِي فَرْحَانَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāma al-maliki wa-hiya naẓunnuhu al-ʿabda wa-hiya farḥānatun
sentences.l: Then when she heard the king's speech — she supposing him the slave — and she being joyful,
sentences.i: Then, hearing the king's words — for she still took him for the slave — and overjoyed,
sentences.n: "نظنه" is printed with ن (1st person, "we suppose") where تظنه (3fs, "she supposes him") is meant — ن and ت are easily confused in this typeface. Rendered per the required sense, "she supposing him."

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي عَلَى رَأْسِي وَعَيْنِي بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā sayyidī ʿalā raʾsī wa-ʿaynī bismillāhi
sentences.l: She said, "O my master: upon my head and my eye! In the name of God."
sentences.i: She said, "O my master, gladly, with all my heart! In the name of God."
sentences.n: "على راسي وعيني" ("upon my head and my eye") is a set idiom of eager compliance, roughly "gladly" or "at once."

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَهَضَتْ وَقَامَتْ وَهِي مَسُرورةٌ تَجْرِي وَ خَرَجَتْ إِلَى الْبِرْكَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma nahaḍat wa-qāmat wa-hiya masrūratun tajrī wa-kharajat ilā al-birkati
sentences.l: Then she rose up and stood, joyful, running, and went out to the pool.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَتْ مِنْ مَائِهَا قَلِيلًا
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhat min māʾihā qalīlan
sentences.l: And she took a little of its water.

sentences.t: فَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرزادَ الْصَبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنْ الْكَلَامِ الْ—
sentences.tr: fa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿan al-kalāmi al—
sentences.l: Then morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent from the speech — the —
sentences.i: But morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent, in the middle of —
sentences.n: The archive itself breaks off here, mid-word, with its own dash: dawn cuts the telling off at this exact point, before the formula that opens the next night resumes it.
